akhfash:4-4.t:
He said ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ﴾: its singular is "العُشَراء" (a she-camel ten months pregnant), like "النُفَسَاء" (a woman in childbed), with "النِفاس" for the plural. And the poet said [in the rajaz metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-eighth verse cited as evidence]:
رُبَّ شريبٍ لَك ذي حُساس * ريانَ يَمْشِي مِشْيَةَ النِّفَاسِ
(Many a drinking-companion of yours, keen of feeling, sated with drink, walks with the gait of women in childbed.)
And "النُّفاس" is also said.

akhfash:6-6.t: And some read ﴿سُجِرِّتْ﴾ (with doubling), and some read it light, citing as proof ﴿وَٱلْبَحْرِ ٱلْمَسْجُورِ﴾. The correct way is the doubling, because when that is "broken" it comes on this pattern: one says "قُطِّعُوا" and "قُبِّلوا", and one does not say of a single person "قُطِّعَ", meaning his hand, nor "قُتِّلَ". «[Translator's note: the source writes «كسر» ("broken") and «يقل»; presumably «كثر» ("multiplied") and «يقال» ("it is said") are meant: the doubled form is used for many subjects.]»

akhfash:8-9.t:
And He said ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ﴾: "وَأَدَهُ" "يَئِدُهُ" "وَأْداً" ("to bury alive"), like "وَعَدَهُ" "يَعِدُهُ" "وَعْداً", the ʿayn (middle radical) being in the manner of a hamza.
And He said ﴿سُئِلَتْ﴾ ﴿بِأَىِّ ذَنبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾; and some read ﴿سَأَلَتْ﴾ — she herself (asked).

akhfash:12-12.t: And He said ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ﴾ light, and some read it heavy (doubled), because its kindling was intensified against them. «[Translator's note: the source writes «جرّها»; presumably «حرّها», "its heat", is meant. The quotation in the source is printed with the doubled form.]»

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿ٱلْجَوَارِ ٱلْكُنَّسِ﴾: its singular is "كانِس", and [the plural]* is "كُنَّس", as you say "عاطِل" and "عُطَّل".

akhfash:24-24.t: And He said ﴿وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى ٱلْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ﴾: He means "that is: stingy" (ببخيل). And some read ﴿بِظَنين﴾, that is: suspected (متَّهَم), because some of the Arabs say "ظننت زيدا", so "هو ظنين", that is: I suspected him, so "he is suspected" (هو مُتَّهَم).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾ is wrapped up and its light taken away,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَإِذَا النُّجُومُ انْكَدَرَتْ﴾ swoop down and fall onto the earth,

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْجِبَالُ سُيِّرَتْ﴾ are taken away from the face of the earth and become scattered dust,

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْعِشَارُ﴾ pregnant she-camels ﴿عُطِّلَتْ﴾ are left without a herdsman, or without milking, because of the calamity that has struck them, though no property was more pleasing to them than they,

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ﴾ are gathered after the resurrection so that retaliation may be taken for some of them against others; then they become dust,

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ﴾ without doubling and with doubling [سُجِرَتْ], are kindled and become fire,

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَإِذَا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ﴾ are joined to their bodies,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْمَوْءُودَةُ﴾ the girl buried alive for fear of shame and want ﴿سُئِلَتْ﴾ to reproach her killer,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿بِأَيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾ it has been read with kasra on the tāʾ, as a reporting of what she is addressed with; and her answer is to say: "I was killed without any sin."

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الصُّحُفُ﴾ the scrolls of deeds ﴿نُشِرَتْ﴾ without doubling and with doubling, are opened and spread out,

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ كُشِطَتْ﴾ is stripped from its places as the skin is stripped from a sheep,

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْجَحِيمُ﴾ the Fire ﴿سُعِّرَتْ﴾ without doubling and with doubling [سُعِرَتْ], is set ablaze,

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَإِذَا الْجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ﴾ is brought near to its people so that they may enter it — the answer (jawāb) of إِذَا at the beginning of the sura and of what is conjoined to it is:

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ﴾ i.e. every soul, at the time of these things mentioned, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿مَا أَحْضَرَتْ﴾ of good and evil.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ﴾ they are the five stars: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus and Mercury. They takhnusu, with ḍamma on the nūn, i.e. go back along their course, behind them: while we see the star at the end of a zodiacal sign, it turns back towards its beginning; and they takinsu, with kasra on the nūn, enter their lairs (kināsihā), i.e. disappear in the places where they disappear.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا عَسْعَسَ﴾ advances with its darkness, or retreats,

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ﴾ extends until it becomes clear daylight,

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ honoured by Allah the Exalted, and he is Gabriel; it is attributed to him because he brought it down,

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿ذِي قُوَّةٍ﴾ i.e. of mighty powers, ﴿عِنْدَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ﴾ i.e. Allah the Exalted, ﴿مَكِينٍ﴾ of high standing; عِنْدَ is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it;

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿مُطَاعٍ ثَمَّ﴾ i.e. the angels in the heavens obey him, ﴿أَمِينٍ﴾ over the revelation.

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وَمَا صَاحِبُكُمْ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ — conjoined to إِنَّهُ to the end of what is sworn upon — ﴿بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾ as you claimed.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ saw Gabriel in the form in which he was created ﴿بِالْأُفُقِ الْمُبِينِ﴾ the clear [horizon], which is the highest, in the direction of the east.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿وَمَا هُوَ﴾ Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿عَلَى الْغَيْبِ﴾ what is hidden of revelation and news of the heaven, ﴿بِظَنِينٍ﴾ suspected; in one reading [بِضَنِينٍ] with ḍād, i.e. miserly, so that he would hold back any of it.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿وَمَا هُوَ﴾ i.e. the Quran ﴿بِقَوْلِ شَيْطَانٍ﴾ who eavesdrops ﴿رَجِيمٍ﴾ stoned.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ﴾ by what path do you go in your denial of the Quran and your turning away from it?

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ﴾ an admonition ﴿لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ mankind and jinn,

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿لِمَنْ شَاءَ مِنْكُمْ﴾ a badal (substitute) for الْعَالَمِينَ, with the preposition repeated, ﴿أَنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ﴾ by following the truth.

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ﴾ uprightness upon the truth ﴿إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ﴾ the creatures, your uprightness upon it.

daas-irab:1-6.t: ﴿إِذَا﴾: a conditional adverb that does not put the verb in the jussive; ﴿الشَّمْسُ﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb explained by the one mentioned after it; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿كُوِّرَتْ﴾: a passive past verb, its deputy agent being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is explicative and has no grammatical position. The verses following it are conjoined to it and their i'rab is the same.

daas-irab:7-9.t: The verse is conjoined to what precedes it, and the one following it is also conjoined. ﴿بِأَيِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) قتلت; ﴿ذَنْبٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿قُتِلَتْ﴾: a passive past verb, its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of سئلت.

daas-irab:10-14.t: The four verses 10–13 are conjoined to what precedes them and their i'rab is clear. ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); ﴿ما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position; ﴿أَحْضَرَتْ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:15-22.t:
﴿فَلا﴾: the fāʾ is a resumptive particle and ﴿لا﴾ is redundant (zāʾida); ﴿أُقْسِمُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿بِالْخُنَّسِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿الْجَوارِ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of الخنس; ﴿الْكُنَّسِ﴾: a second adjective. ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ﴾: conjoined to الخنس; ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of time; ﴿عَسْعَسَ﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation (iḍāfa).
﴿وَالصُّبْحِ إِذا تَنَفَّسَ﴾: conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لَقَوْلُ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and ﴿قول﴾ is the khabar (predicate) of inna; the nominal clause is the answer to the oath; ﴿رَسُولٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿كَرِيمٍ﴾: adjective; ﴿ذِي﴾: a second adjective of رسول; ﴿قُوَّةٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿عِنْدَ﴾: an adverb of place; ﴿ذِي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿الْعَرْشِ﴾: also muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿مَكِينٍ﴾: a third adjective of رسول; ﴿مُطاعٍ﴾: a fourth adjective; ﴿ثَمَّ﴾: an adverb of place meaning "there"; ﴿أَمِينٍ﴾: a fifth adjective of رسول. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿ما﴾ is negative, working like laysa; ﴿صاحِبُكُمْ﴾: its noun; ﴿بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾: genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ما.

daas-irab:23-26.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is a particle of oath and of the genitive, the lām occurs in the answer to the oath, and ﴿قد﴾ is a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿رَآهُ﴾: a past verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is the answer to the oath and has no grammatical position; ﴿بِالْأُفُقِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿الْمُبِينِ﴾: naʿt (adjective) of الأفق.
﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); ﴿وَما﴾: the Ḥijāzī negative mā; ﴿هُوَ﴾: its noun; ﴿عَلَى الْغَيْبِ﴾: attached to what follows them; ﴿بِضَنِينٍ﴾: genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction and ﴿ما﴾ is Ḥijāzī; ﴿هُوَ﴾: its noun; ﴿بِقَوْلِ﴾: genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of ما; ﴿شَيْطانٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿رَجِيمٍ﴾: adjective; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَأَيْنَ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and ﴿أين﴾ is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as an adverb of place; ﴿تَذْهَبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:27-29.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾: negative; ﴿هُوَ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject); ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿ذِكْرٌ﴾: khabar (predicate); ﴿لِلْعالَمِينَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿لِمَنْ﴾: badal (substitute) for His words للعالمين; ﴿شاءَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾: attached to the verb; ﴿أَنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, the agent being latent; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is the object of شاء. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) and ﴿ما﴾ is negative; ﴿تَشاؤُنَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its agent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception; ﴿أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative by an, and the Name of Majesty is its agent; ﴿رَبُّ الْعالَمِينَ﴾: badal, muḍāf to العالمين; the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by annexation to an adverb of time, the implied form being: "وقت أن يشاء الله" (at the time that Allah wills).

dervis-irab:1-14.t:
* Vocabulary:
(كُوِّرَتْ) it was wrapped up and its light taken away. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "كار الرجل العمامة كورا, of the pattern قال: he wound the turban around his head. Every turn is a كور, named by the maṣdar (verbal noun); its plural is أكوار, like ثوب and أثواب. كوّرها, with doubling, is intensive; and from it one says كورت الشيء when you wrap it in a circular manner. The saying of the Exalted إذا الشمس كوّرت means: it was rolled up like the rolling up of a scroll." Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: "There are two views on التكوير. It may be from كورت العمامة when you wind it, i.e. its light is wrapped up so that its spreading and diffusion over the horizons goes away; this is an expression for removing it and taking it away, because as long as it remains, its light is spread out and not wrapped up. Or its wrapping may be an expression for lifting it up and covering it, because when a garment is to be put away it is wrapped and folded; similar to it is His saying: يوم نطوي السماء. Or it may be from طعنه فجوّره وكوّره, when he throws him down, i.e. it is thrown and cast down from its orbit, just as the stars were described with الانكدار." What the lexicons have set out can be summarized as follows: "كار يكور كورا العمامة على رأسه: he wound it and wrapped it around; كور الله الليل على النهار: He made this enter into that; كورت الشمس: its light was gathered and wrapped as the turban is wrapped; it has been said: it faded away and departed."
(انْكَدَرَتْ) they fell and dropped onto the earth. The basic sense of الانكدار is pouring down. Abū ʿUbayda said: انكدرت means they swooped down, as the eagle swoops down when it folds its wings. Al-ʿAjjāj said, describing a falcon:
أبصر حرمات فلاة فانكدر ... تقصي البازي إذا البازي كسر
(He caught sight of the forbidden creatures of a desert and swooped down, as the hawk swoops when the hawk folds its wings.)
(الْعِشارُ) pregnant she-camels, the plural of عشراء, like نفاس as the plural of نفساء. She is the one whose pregnancy has reached ten months; that then remains her name until she gives birth at the completion of the year, and she is the most precious thing her owners have. It is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ passed among his Companions by some pregnant she-camels and lowered his gaze. It was said to him: "These are the most precious of our wealth; why do you not look at them?" He said: "Allah has forbidden me that," then recited: ولا تمدنّ عينيك (the verse).
(سُجِّرَتْ) سجر يسجر سجرا, of the pattern نصر, التنور: he filled the oven with fuel and heated it; سجر الماء النهر: the water filled the river; سجر البحر: the sea overflowed; سجر الماء في حلقه: he poured it; سجر الكلب: he tied the dog with the ساجور (collar); سجر الشيء: he let it loose. This is what the lexicons have mentioned regarding this root. In al-Asās: "كلب مسجور, مسجّر and مسوجر; I سجرته, سجّرته and سوجرته: I put the ساجور on him, which is an iron collar studded with nails with sharp points. بحر مسجور and مسجّر, and عين مسجورة and مسجّرة: brim-full. سجر السيل الآبار والأحساء (the torrent filled the wells and the water-pits); 'We passed by every حاجر and ساجر', which is every place a torrent has passed and filled. سجر التنور: he filled it with سجور, which is its fuel; and he سجره with the مسجرة, which is the poker. Of the figurative usages: سجرت الناقة سجرا and سجّرت تسجيرا: the she-camel drew out her yearning cry after her young one and filled her mouth with it. He said:
حنّت إلى برك فقلت لها: قرّي ... بعض الحنين فإن سجرك شائقي
(She yearned for a herd of camels, and I said to her: hold back some of your yearning, for your yearning cry stirs my longing.)
And from it: ساجرته مساجرة, which is close friendship and intermixing; he is my سجير and they are my سجراء, because each of the two yearns for the other. And from it: ماء أسجر, water mixed with turbidity and redness from rainwater; one says: 'There is سجرة in it', 'it is أسجر', 'a قطرة سجراء (reddish drop)', and 'عين سجراء'. Al-Ḥuwaydira said:
بغريض سارية أدرّته الصبا ... من ماء أسجر أطيب المستنقع
(With fresh water of a night-cloud which the east wind made flow, from reddish water, the sweetest of pools.)
عين سجراء: [an eye] whose white is mixed with redness; 'There is سجرة in your eye'; and 'on their necks are السواجير', i.e. the fetters." Something of the meaning of this root has already passed in al-Ṭūr. Accordingly, the views on what is meant by it here are many. Al-Qurṭubī, as is his habit, counted the views on it, and we point to them briefly:
1- وإذا البحار سجرت: i.e. they were filled with water, so that some of them overflow into others and they become one thing.
2- It has been said: their fresh water was let loose upon their salt water until they were filled.
3- It has been said: they became one sea.
4- It has been said: they dried up, so that not one drop of their water remains.
5- It has been said: they were set alight and became fire.
6- It has been said: it is the redness of their water, until it becomes as though it were blood.
(الْمَوْؤُدَةُ) He said in al-Asās: "وأد ابنته: he weighed her down with earth. «وإذا الموءودة سئلت». Al-Farazdaq said:
وجدي الذي منع الوائدات ... وأحيا الوئيد فلم يوأد
(And my grandfather is the one who stopped the women who buried girls alive, and gave life to the buried girl, so that she was not buried.)"
وأد ابنته يئدها, of the pattern ضرب: he buried her in the earth while she was alive; so the daughter is وئيد, وئيدة and موءودة. Al-Zamakhsharī said in al-Kashshāf: "وأد يئد is a metathesis (maqlūb) of آد يئود, when it weighs down. Allah the Exalted said: ولا يئوده حفظهما. [It is so called] because it is weighing down with earth." Abū Ḥayyān followed this up in al-Baḥr and said: "It cannot be claimed of وأد that it is a metathesis of آد, because each of the two is fully conjugated in the past, the imperative, the imperfect, the maṣdar, the active participle and the passive participle, and there is nothing in it of the grounds that justify claiming metathesis. What tells originality apart from metathesis is that one of the two arrangements has a rule that testifies to its originality while the other does not; or that it is free of augment letters while the other has an augment; or that it is more fully conjugated while the other is not; or that it is more frequently used than the other — this being as established and settled in the science of morphology. The first is like يئس and أيس, the second like طأمن and اطمأن, the third like شوائع and شواع, and the fourth like لعمري and رعملي."

* I'rab:
(إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ) (إذا) is a future adverb containing the meaning of condition; its apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), in the twelve places where it occurs, is His saying (علمت نفس), as will come, and it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to its apodosis. (الشمس) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an implied verb explained by what follows. Al-Zamakhsharī inclined to this and disallowed its being nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), because إذا calls for a verb on account of the meaning of condition in it; but what al-Zamakhsharī disallowed — a mubtadaʾ occurring after it — the Kufans and al-Akhfash among the Basrans permitted. The clause (كورت) is explicative and has no grammatical position.
(وَإِذَا النُّجُومُ انْكَدَرَتْ) conjoined to what preceded and parsed like it; but (النجوم) here is the fāʿil (agent) of a verb explained by His saying (انكدرت).
(وَإِذَا الْجِبالُ سُيِّرَتْ، وَإِذَا الْعِشارُ عُطِّلَتْ) also conjoined. (الجبال) and (العشار) are the deputy agents of an omitted verb. The meaning of their being left idle is their being left without a herdsman and without milking, on account of the calamity that has befallen them.
(وَإِذَا الْوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ) also conjoined.
(وَإِذَا الْبِحارُ سُجِّرَتْ وَإِذَا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ) also conjoined. The meaning is: the spirits were returned to their bodies; this is based on التزويج meaning making a thing a pair, with النفوس on this view meaning the spirits. It has also been said: every person is coupled with his party and every like with its like, so the righteous man is coupled with the righteous man in Paradise.
(وَإِذَا الْمَوْؤُدَةُ سُئِلَتْ بِأَيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ) also conjoined. (بأي) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (قتلت), and the clause stands in place of the second object of (سئلت). When a daughter was born to one of the Arabs and he let her live, he would dress her in a garment of wool or hair and leave her to herd the camels and sheep. If he wanted to kill her, he would leave her until, when she was six years old, he would say to her mother: "Perfume her and adorn her, so that I may take her to her in-laws." He would have dug a pit or a well in the desert; he would take her to it and say to her: "Look into it," then push her from behind and heap earth upon her until the well was level with the ground. Al-Farazdaq — Abū Firās Hammām ibn Ghālib ibn Ṣaʿṣaʿa — boasted of his grandfather Ṣaʿṣaʿa, since he had prevented the burying alive of daughters, as has preceded.
(وَإِذَا الصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ وَإِذَا السَّماءُ كُشِطَتْ وَإِذَا الْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ وَإِذَا الْجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ) also conjoined to what preceded.
(عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما أَحْضَرَتْ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of (إذا), as has preceded. (علمت نفس) is a past verb and its fāʿil, (ما) is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause (أحضرت) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of (ما).

* Rhetoric:
Indefiniteness (al-tankīr):
In His saying «علمت نفس ما أحضرت» there is indefiniteness in (نفس), and its benefit is generality. An objector may object that an indefinite noun conveys generality only when it is in the context of negation; accordingly, here it occurs in the context of affirmation, where it is for singularity or for kind — so how can singularity or kind agree with a setting suited to generality? The answer to this objection is that what was mentioned about its being in the context of negation and affirmation is a general tendency, not a universal rule, so it does not preclude generality sometimes being intended by it with the help of the setting. There is another answer to this objection: the indefinite noun here occurs in the context of a condition, and the context of a condition is like [that of negation] [Translator's note: the source has كسياق النكرة, apparently for كسياق النفي] in that the indefinite noun is for generality when it occurs in either of them.

dervis-irab:15-29.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بِالْخُنَّسِ) الخنس: all the stars, or only the planets among them, or some of them; from الخنس, which is going back, because they go back in their course behind them. The verb is خنس يخنس, of the pattern دخل. In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: "الخنس are all the stars, because they recede (تخنس) at setting and because they are hidden by day; and it is said: they are the planets among them, to the exclusion of the fixed stars." Al-Farrāʾ said on the saying of the Exalted فلا أقسم بالخنس الجواري الكنس that they are the five stars: Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus and Mercury, because they recede in their course and withdraw (تكنس) as gazelles withdraw into their lairs. الخنس is also the shelter of gazelles, and the gazelles themselves, and wild cows.
(الْكُنَّسِ) In al-Miṣbāḥ: "كناس الظبي, with kasra, is the gazelle's dwelling; كنس الظبي كنوسا, of the pattern نزل: it entered its lair; تكنس الظبي: it went out of sight and hid in its lair; تكنس الرجل: he entered the tent; تكنست المرأة: she entered the litter (al-hawdaj)."
(عَسْعَسَ) it advanced with its darkness, or retreated. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
حتى إذا الصبح لها تنفسا ... وانجاب عنها ليلها وعسعسا
(Until, when the morning breathed for her, and her night was rent away from her and departed.)

* I'rab:
(فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ، الْجَوارِ الْكُنَّسِ، وَاللَّيْلِ إِذا عَسْعَسَ، وَالصُّبْحِ إِذا تَنَفَّسَ) The fāʾ is resumptive. The discussion of (لا) has preceded, so refresh your memory of it. (أقسم) is an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anā". (بالخنس) is attached (mutaʿalliq) to (أقسم). (الجواري) is a naʿt (adjective) or badal (substitute), and (الكنس) is a naʿt of (الجواري). (والليل): the wāw is also for the oath; (الليل) is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "أقسم". (إذا) is an adverb attached to the verb of oath, and the clause (عسعس) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. (والصبح إذا تنفس) is conjoined to the preceding clause. We did not conjoin (الليل) to (الخنس) only because the wāw is the beginning of [a new] oath.
If it is said: "Then you have contradicted Sībawayh, for he does not regard the wāw that follows an oath as the beginning of an oath, but as a conjunction; and you have made the first wāw, which follows an oath, the beginning of an oath?" We say: Sībawayh spoke only about the wāw [of oath]; as for the verse, the first oath in it is with the bāʾ and the verb, so we made the wāw after that an oath and a follower; and that is more eloquent, as though He swore by two different things.
If it is said: "Indeed, Sībawayh spoke only about the wāw that follows an oath; so what is the difference between a wāw that follows an oath made with the wāw and a wāw that follows an oath made with the bāʾ, when they are nothing but the same? For each of them is an instrument for it, and the tāʾ indicates the bāʾ, so their rule is one." We say: they are not the same. When the oath begins with the wāw and is followed by another wāw, making the other an oath involves a distasteful repetition, since the instrument is one. That is not so in the verse, since the instrument differs, so the [distasteful] effect of repetition is then avoided. Do you not see that if the oath began with the wāw and was then followed by an oath with the bāʾ, it would be necessary to make them two independent oaths? So likewise if this order were reversed. Moreover, if what prevented Sībawayh from making the second wāw an independent oath was that the apodosis comes as a single one and that the first wāw would need something omitted, while conjunction makes the assumption of an omitted element unnecessary — then this does not necessarily extend to the bāʾ, because it is the root of the oath, especially with the verb of oath stated explicitly and then emphasized by the addition of (لا); for in all of that together there is what makes it unnecessary to give it its own stated apodosis. That is not so with the wāw, for its standing in the oath is weak in comparison with the bāʾ. So it does not follow from the omission of an apodosis whose indication is firmly established that an apodosis less clear than it may be omitted.
We close the discussion of this question with an excellent subtle point: I restricted the raising of the question to the second wāw, in His saying (والليل إذا عسعس), and not the third, because it does not apply to it. Do you not see that if you made it a conjunction you would not be committed to conjoining onto two governors, because you would make it stand in for the bāʾ and make (إذا) in it accusative directly by the verb, since no adverb preceded in the verb's clause onto which (إذا) could be conjoined? It then becomes like your saying مررت بزيد وعمرو اليوم (I passed by Zayd and ʿAmr today): (اليوم) is accusative directly by the verb, and it is understood from the example that your passing by Zayd is unrestricted, not qualified by an adverb, and that only your passing by ʿAmr in particular is qualified by (اليوم). But [does this] match the verse? For the adverb in it, even though the verb governs it directly, qualifies the oath by the night, not the oath by الخنس.
(إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of the oath. (إنّ) and its noun; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (قول) is its khabar (predicate), (رسول) is muḍāf ilayhi, and (كريم) is a naʿt. What is meant by it will come in the section on Benefits.
(ذِي قُوَّةٍ عِنْدَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ مَكِينٍ مُطاعٍ ثَمَّ أَمِينٍ) (ذي قوة) is a second adjective of (رسول). (عند ذي العرش) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (مسكين) [Translator's note: so in the source; read مكين], because it was originally an adjective of it, and when it was placed first it became accusative as a ḥāl. (مكين) is a third adjective and (مطاع) a fourth adjective. (ثم) is an adverb meaning "there", attached to (مطاع). (أمين) is a fifth adjective.
(وَما صاحِبُكُمْ بِمَجْنُونٍ) The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause is conjoined to (إنه لقول رسول كريم). (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative ما, (صاحبكم) is its noun, the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and (مجنون) is genitive in form, accusative in position, as the khabar of (ما).
(وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالْأُفُقِ الْمُبِينِ) conjoined to His saying (إنه لقول …), so it falls within the scope of what is sworn. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath, (قد) is a particle of realization, (رآه) is a past verb with a latent fāʿil [and its object], (بالأفق) is attached to (رآه), and (المبين) is a naʿt of (الأفق).
(وَما هُوَ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ) also conjoined. (ما) is the Ḥijāzī negative ما and (هو) its noun; (على الغيب) is attached to (ضنين); the bāʾ is a redundant preposition, and (ضنين) is genitive in form, accusative in position, as the khabar of (ما). (على) means the bāʾ, i.e. he does not withhold it from you but informs you of it. It was also read بظنين, with the dotted ẓāʾ, i.e. suspected. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "الظنة, with kasra, is suspicion; it is a noun from ظننته, of the pattern قتل, when you suspected him; so he is ظنين, a faʿīl in the sense of a passive participle (mafʿūl). Among the Seven [readings]: وما هو على الغيب بظنين, i.e. suspected." Also in al-Miṣbāḥ: "ضن بالشيء يضنّ, of the pattern تعب, ضنا and ضنّة with kasra and ضنانة with fatḥa: he was miserly, so he is miserly; and the pattern ضرب is a dialectal variant of it."
(وَما هُوَ بِقَوْلِ شَيْطانٍ رَجِيمٍ) also conjoined; it is a negation of their saying that it is soothsaying and sorcery.
(فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction. (أين) is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place, vague rather than specific, attached to (تذهبون). (تذهبون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative and its fāʿil; i.e. which road are you taking?
(إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعالَمِينَ لِمَنْ شاءَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ) (إن) is negative, (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (إلا) is a particle of restriction, and (ذكر) is the khabar. (للعالمين) is attached to (ذكر) or is a naʿt of it. (لمن) is a badal from His saying (للعالمين), with repetition of the governor, which is the lām. The clause (شاء) has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of (من); (منكم) is a ḥāl; and (أن) with what is in its scope is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of (شاء).
(وَما تَشاؤُنَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعالَمِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction, (ما) is negative, (تشاءون) is an imperfect verb in the nominative and the wāw is its fāʿil, and (إلا) is a particle of restriction. (أن) and what follows it are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the [implied] preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (تشاءون). (الله) is the fāʿil, and (رب العالمين) is a badal or naʿt of (الله). Al-Bayḍāwī preferred making the interpreted maṣdar accusative as an adverb (ẓarfiyya); his wording: "And you do not will uprightness, O you who will it, except that Allah wills — i.e. except at the time that Allah wills your willing; so to Him belongs the favour, and the right is upon you for your uprightness."

* Benefits:
The exegetes differed. A great multitude of them held that what is meant by the noble messenger here, down to the last of the attributes, is Muḥammad ﷺ; if the matter is so, that is Allah's customary favour upon His Prophet. A great multitude of them also held that what is meant by it is Jibrīl, upon him be peace. Disagreement has arisen over the relative merit of the angels and the messengers. The well-known position of Abū al-Ḥasan al-Ashʿarī is to prefer the messengers, and the doctrine of the Muʿtazila is to prefer the angels. However, those who differed agreed that it is not permissible to prefer either of the two exalted groups in a way that implies disparaging a specific one of the angels or a specific one of the messengers, because even though preference is established, specifying [the one surpassed] is hurtful to the one surpassed. On this the skilled scholars interpreted his saying ﷺ: "Do not prefer me over Yūnus ibn Mattā," i.e. do not specify one surpassed in particular; for preference in general is established by the consensus of the Muslims, i.e. the preference of the Prophet ﷺ over all the prophets together. Ibn Fāris, may Allah have mercy on him, used to clarify this with an example, saying: if you said in the presence of a group of jurists, "So-and-so is the best of the people of his age," the group would bear this preference, even though it entails their inclusion among those surpassed; but if you specified one of them and said, "So-and-so is better than you," the hurt would quickly reach some of you.
Al-Qāḍī al-Bayḍāwī said: "It has been used as evidence for the superiority of Jibrīl over Muḥammad, upon both of them be blessing and peace, since He enumerated the excellences of Jibrīl and limited Himself to denying madness of him ﷺ. That is weak, since what is intended by it is to refute their saying 'it is only a human being who teaches him' and 'has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?', not to enumerate their merits and weigh them against each other."
As for al-Karkhī, he said: "Then, if you look closely, you will realize that applying those attributes to Jibrīl in this setting is an insertion (idmāj) of the glorification of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that he reached such standing and loftiness of rank with the Lord of the Throne that the envoy between Him and him was made one like this angel, brought near, obeyed and trustworthy. So the statement of these attributes, with respect to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, is an elevation of rank for him, just like the statement 'with the Lord of the Throne' with respect to the elevation of the rank of Jibrīl, upon him be peace."
As for al-Zamakhsharī, he produced something which perhaps Jibrīl, Allah's blessings be upon him, would not have been pleased with, a shortcoming in the right of the bearer of good news and the warner, by saying: "This suffices you as evidence of the standing of Jibrīl, upon him be peace, and his superiority over the angels, and of the difference from the rank of the best of humans, Muḥammad ﷺ, if you weigh the two mentions when He paired them, and compare His saying: إنه لقول رسول كريم، ذي قوة عند ذي العرش مكين، مطاع ثم أمين with His saying: وما صاحبكم بمجنون."
Ibn al-Munayyir, as is his habit, refuted al-Zamakhsharī, saying: "Then the discussion returns to the verse, after granting that Jibrīl is meant and after we entrust to Allah [the reckoning for] his specifying the Prophet ﷺ and counting him the one surpassed. We say: no attribute is mentioned in it but the Prophet ﷺ has its like. The first of them is رسول كريم; He said with respect to him ﷺ at the end of Sūrat al-Ḥāqqa: إنه لقول رسول كريم. It has also been said that Jibrīl is meant there, but His saying وما هو بقول شاعر rejects that, and al-Zamakhsharī agreed with that earlier. So this is the first of the attributes [Translator's note: the source has الفوت, apparently for النعوت] and the greatest of them. As for His saying ذي قوة, it is not the point of dispute, since there is no contention that Jibrīl, upon him be peace, has superiority in bodily strength; whoever uproots cities with a feather of his wing — there is no disputing the superiority of his strength over the strength of humans; this has been said in explaining His saying ذو مرة فاستوى. As for His saying عند ذي العرش مكين مطاع ثم أمين, the obedience of the angels has also been established [Translator's note: the source prints نبتت for ثبتت] for our Prophet ﷺ. It has come that Jibrīl, upon him be peace, said to the Prophet: 'Allah conveys greetings of peace to you, and He has ordered the angel of the mountains to obey you,' when Quraysh harmed him; so the angel greeted him and said: 'If you order me to bring the two mountains (al-Akhshabān) together upon them, I will do it'; but the Prophet ﷺ was patient and sought the reward. The greatest and noblest of that is his Praised Station in the Great Intercession, on the day when no one goes before him, when Allah the Exalted will say to him: 'Raise your head; speak and you will be heard; ask and you will be given; intercede and your intercession will be accepted.' As for أمين, he said: 'By Allah, I am trustworthy on earth and trustworthy in heaven.' And sufficient for you is His saying وما هو على الغيب بظنين: if you read it with the ẓāʾ, its meaning is that he ﷺ is trustworthy over the unseen and not suspected; and if you read it with the ḍād, it goes back to generosity. So how can one argue for preference by means of attributes shared equally by the superior and the surpassed?"

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «والليل إذا عسعس والصبح إذا تنفس» there is an implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya). He likened the night to a person who advances and retreats, then omitted the thing compared to [Translator's note: the source says المشبه (the thing compared), though in an implicit metaphor it is the المشبه به that is omitted] and took one of its attributes, namely the word عسعس, i.e. it advanced and retreated. Likewise He likened the morning to a living being that breathes, omitted [the thing compared to], and brought one of its attributes, namely breathing, i.e. the exit of breath from the interior. Or it may be said that He likened the night to a distressed, grieving person who is confined so that he does not move; when he breathes, he finds his relief. Here, when the morning rises, it is as though it has been entirely freed from grief, so that was expressed by breathing.
2- In His saying «فلا أقسم بالخنس الجوار الكنس» there is the device of al-iltizām (self-imposed constraint), for the nūn is kept before the sīn.

farraa:1-1.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِذَا ٱلشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾: its light is gone.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: [128/a] ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلنُّجُومُ ٱنكَدَرَتْ﴾.
That is: they scattered and fell on the face of the earth.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْعِشَارُ عُطِّلَتْ﴾.
العشار: the pregnant she-camels; their owners abandon them, being occupied with themselves.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ Sallām ibn Sulaym narrated to me from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq from ʿIkrima, who said: their gathering is their death.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْبِحَارُ سُجِّرَتْ﴾.
They opened into one another and became one sea.

farraa:7-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلنُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ Sallām ibn Sulaym narrated to me from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq Abū Sufyān from ʿIkrima, concerning His saying: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلنُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ﴾. He said: the man is paired in Paradise with his righteous companion of this world, and the man who used to do evil deeds is paired in the Fire with his companion who used to help him in that; that is the pairing of the souls. Al-Farrāʾ said: I heard one of the Arabs say: زوّجت إبلي (I paired my camels); and Allah forbade pairing two together — that is, tying one camel to another so that they feed together and travel together.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān narrated to me from al-Kalbī from Abū Ṣāliḥ from his father from Ibn ʿAbbās; and ʿAlī ibn Ghurāb narrated to me from Ibn Mujāhid from his father from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ بِأَىِّ ذَنبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, identical to the standard reading; Ibn ʿAbbās's reported reading is «سَأَلَتْ … قُتِلْتُ», which the following remarks presuppose], and he said: she is the one who asks and is not asked. It is also permissible to read: ﴿بِأىِّ ذَنبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾ with the meaning: for what sin was I killed (قُتِلْتُ), as you say in speech: ʿAbd Allāh — for what sin was he beaten (ضُرِبَ), and: for what sin was I beaten (ضُرِبْتُ). Parallels to this from reported speech (ḥikāya) have already been mentioned; of that kind is [128/b] the saying of ʿAntara:
الشاتِمى عِرضى ولم أشتمها * والناذرين إذا لقيتهما دمى
(The two who revile my honour though I did not revile them, and who vowed my blood if I met them.)
The meaning is: the two of them used to say: "If we meet ʿAntara we will surely kill him." So the speech ran in his poem according to this meaning, while the wording differs. Likewise his saying:
رَجْلان من ضَبة أخبرانا * إنا رأينا رجلا عريانا
(Two men of Ḍabba informed us: "We saw a naked man.")
The meaning is: they informed us that they [had seen]; but it ran according to the manner of direct speech, as one says: ʿAbd Allāh said: إنه لذاهب (he is going) and إني ذاهب (I am going), the going being his in both ways.
Whoever reads: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ﴾ has two interpretations in it. سُئلت: she was asked, and it was said to her: ﴿بِأَىِّ ذَنب قُتلتِ﴾ (for what sin were you killed?); then قُتلتْ is permissible, just as it was permissible in the first question. Or سُئلت may mean: those who buried her alive were asked about her, as though you said: she was demanded of them, and it was said: "Where are your children? And for what sin did you kill them?" All the interpretations are good and clear, except that (سُئلتْ) is the more common, so it is the dearest of them to me.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ﴾.
Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and his companions read it with shadda, and others of the people of Medina and elsewhere read it lightened. Both are correct. Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿صُحُفاً مُّنَشَّرَةً﴾, and this is evidence for whoever reads with shadda; and منشورة is [good] Arabic. The doubling and the lightening are [both possible] in it because of its multitude and because it is a plural, as you say: مررت بكباشٍ مذبّحةٍ and مذبوحةٍ (I passed by slaughtered rams). When it is singular, only the lightened form is permissible, as you say: رجل مقتول (a slain man), and you do not say مُقَتَّل.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلسَّمَآءُ كُشِطَتْ﴾.
It was stripped off and folded up. In [129/a] the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "قشطت" with qāf; they are two dialectal forms. The Arabs say القافور and الكافور (camphor), and القَفّ and الكَفّ. When two letters are close in their point of articulation, they alternate in the dialects, as one says جدف and جدث (grave); fāʾ and thāʾ alternate in much of the language, as was said: الأثافي and الأثاثي [«الأثائى» in the source] (hearth-stones), and ثوب فُرْقبي and ثُرقبي (a kind of garment), and وقعوا في عاثور شرّ and عافور شرّ (they fell into a pit of evil).

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and his companions read it lightened, and the others with shadda.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ مَّآ أَحْضَرَتْ ﴾.
It is the response (jawāb) to His saying: ﴿إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾ (1) and to what comes after it. ﴿وَإِذَا الْجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ﴾ (13): it was brought near.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلْخُنَّسِ﴾.
They are the five stars [planets] that recede (تخنس) in their course, then return, and تكنس: they hide, as gazelles hide (تكنس) in caves, which is the كِناس (lair). The five are: Bahrām [Mars], Zuḥal [Saturn], ʿUṭārid [Mercury], al-Zuhara [Venus] and al-Mushtarī [Jupiter].
Al-Kalbī said: al-Birjīs, meaning al-Mushtarī.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذَا عَسْعَسَ﴾.
The exegetes agreed that the meaning of "عسعس" is: it turned away. One of our companions used to claim that عسعس means: its beginning drew near and it grew dark. Abū al-Bilād the grammarian used to recite concerning it:
عَسْعَسَ حتى لو يشاءُ ادّنا * كان له من ضوئهِ مَقْبسُ
(It drew on [the night] until, if he wished, when he drew near, he would have a firebrand from its light.)
He means: إذ دنا (when he drew near); then he drops the hamza of إذ and assimilates the dhāl into the dāl. They used to consider this verse to be fabricated.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلصُّبْحِ إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ﴾.
When the day rises high, that is the breathing of the morning.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَريمٍ﴾.
He means Gabriel, may Allah bless him and all the prophets.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى ٱلْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ﴾ [129/b].
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad narrated to us, saying:] al-Farrāʾ narrated to us, saying: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from ʿĀṣim ibn Abī al-Najūd from Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh, who said: You read (بضنين), "with a miser", and we read (بظنين), "with one suspected". ʿĀṣim, the people of the Ḥijāz and Zayd ibn Thābit read (بضنين), and it is good. He says: the unseen of heaven comes to him, and he is begrudged in it (منفوس فيه), yet he does not withhold it from you. If in place of على there were عن, it would be acceptable, or the bāʾ, as you say: ما هو بضنين بالغيب (he is not miserly with the unseen). Those who said بظنين argued that على strengthens their view, as you say: ما أنت على فلان بمتهم (you are not suspected regarding So-and-so). And you say: ما هو على الغيب بظنين, i.e. not weak — He says: he is capable of bearing it. The Arabs say of a weak man or of a scanty thing: هو ظنون. I heard one of Quḍāʿa say: "The weak one (الظنون) may guide you to the right opinion", meaning the weak among men. If the meaning of ظنين is "weak", it is as was said: ماءٌ شريب and شروب (drinkable water), and قروني and قريني (my self/my resolve); and I heard: قروني and قريني, and قرونتي and قرينتي — except that the preferred way is not to add the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa]. And ناقة طعوم and طعيم, which is the one between lean and fat.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ﴾.
The Arabs say: إلى أين تذهب? (to where are you going?) and أين تذهب? (where are you going?). They say: ذهبت الشامَ (I went to Syria), ذهبت السوقَ (I went to the market), انطلقت الشامَ, انطلقت السوقَ, and خرجت الشامَ — we have heard it with these three words: خرجت, انطلقت and ذهبت. Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard the Arabs say: انطُلِقَ به الفورَ (he was taken off at once), putting it in the accusative on the sense of dropping the preposition (ilqāʾ al-ṣifa). One of Banū ʿUqayl recited to me:
تَصيحُ بنا حَنيفةُ إذ رأتنا * وأىّ الأرض تذهبُ للصِّياح
(Ḥanīfa shout at us when they see us — and to what land would you go at the shouting?)
He means: إلى أيّ الأرض تذهب (to which land would you go) [130/a]. They allowed dropping (إلى) with these words because they use them so much.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «إذا»: adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) its apodosis {عَلِمَتْ} in verse (14); «الشمس»: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an implied verb explained by what follows it, and the clause «كُوِّرت» is explicative; and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «النجوم»: fāʿil (agent) of an implied verb explained by what follows it, and the clause «انكدرت» is explicative; and the clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis is conjoined to the initial one, with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: (بأي ذنب قتلت) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قُتِلت», and the clause «قُتلت» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb of asking, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «علمت» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The fāʾ is resumptive, and the clause «لا أقسم» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: «الجوار»: badal (substitute) of «الخُنَّس», genitive (majrūr) with the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the omitted yāʾ; «الكُنَّس» is a naʿt (adjective) of «للجوار».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: His saying «والليل»: a noun conjoined to «الخُنَّس»; «إذا»: a pure adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) {أُقْسِمُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: (إنه لقول رسول كريم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam).

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «ذي»: naʿt (adjective) of {رَسُولٍ}; «عند»: an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مكين»; «مكين»: naʿt of {رَسُولٍ}.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: «مطاع»: second naʿt (adjective); «ثم»: an adverb indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مطاع»; «أمين» is a third naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: (وما صاحبكم بمجنون) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam) in verse (19), and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما», which operates like laysa.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: The wāw is a conjunction, and the clause «لقد رآه» is conjoined to the clause {وَمَا صَاحِبُكُمْ بِمَجْنُونٍ}; the lām is that of the oath; the preposition «بالأفق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «رآه».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: (وما هو على الغيب بضنين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is conjoined to the clause {رَآهُ}, and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: The interrogative clause is resumptive, and «أين»: an interrogative noun, an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «تذهبون».

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: (إن هو إلا ذكر للعالمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; «إن» is negating and «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the preposition «للعالمين» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ذكر».

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: The preposition «لمن» is a badal (substitute) of {لِلْعَالَمِينَ}; the preposition «منكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «شاء»; and the maṣdar (verbal noun) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: (وما تشاءون إلا أن يشاء الله رب العالمين) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «إلا» is for restriction (ḥaṣr); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is accusative by removal of the preposition, the bāʾ; «رب» is a badal (substitute).

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (إذا الشمس كورت): the discussion of the nominative of what follows (إذا) has already preceded, in al-Mursalāt and elsewhere.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t: His saying (مطاع ثم): (ثم) is an adverbial of place (ẓarf makān).

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying (على الغيب بضنين): the entry of (على) indicates that (ضنين) with ḍād means "miserly"; one says "I was miserly toward him" (بخلت عليه). Had it been with ẓāʾ [(بظنين)], meaning "suspected" [Translator's note: printed «منهم», read as «متهم»], it would have been with bāʾ, as one says "he is suspected of (بـ) such-and-such", and one does not say "of (على) such-and-such". (على) may also be in the place of the bāʾ, in which case the reading with ẓāʾ is good.
His saying (إلا أن يشاء الله): (أن) is in the position of the genitive with an implied bāʾ, or in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition.

mekki-muskil:26-26.t: His saying (فأين تذهبون): it should properly be with (إلى), because (ذهب) is intransitive; its implied form is "To where are you going?" But (إلى) was omitted, as they said "I went the Levant", i.e. to the Levant, and "I went out the market", i.e. to the market. Sībawayh reported of this only "I went the Levant", i.e. to the Levant, and "I entered the house", i.e. into the house. (أين) is an adverbial of place.

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿مطاع﴾: a fourth naʿt (adjective) of ﴿رسول﴾, genitive (majrūr).
﴿ثم﴾: an adverb of place meaning "there", indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مطاع﴾.
﴿أمين﴾: a fifth naʿt of ﴿رسول﴾, genitive.

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negative mā, which works like laysa.
﴿صاحبكم﴾: the noun (ism) of ﴿ما﴾, and the attached pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿بمجنون﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿مجنون﴾ is the predicate (khabar) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative (manṣūb) by position and genitive by the bāʾ in form. The clause is conjoined to His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنه لقول رسول كريم﴾.

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿ولقد﴾: conjoined to ﴿إنه لقول رسول كريم﴾; the lām is the answer to the omitted oath, and qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq).
﴿رآه﴾: a past verb, with a latent (mustatir) fāʿil (agent), and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿بالأفق﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿رآه﴾.
﴿المبين﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿الأفق﴾.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negative mā, which works like laysa.
﴿هو﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of ﴿ما﴾.
﴿على الغيب﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ضنين﴾.
﴿بضنين﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿ضنين﴾ is the predicate (khabar) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative by position and genitive by the bāʾ in form.

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿ما﴾ is the Ḥijāzī negative mā, which works like laysa.
﴿هو﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as the noun (ism) of ﴿ما﴾.
﴿بقول﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and ﴿قول﴾ is the predicate (khabar) of the Ḥijāzī ﴿ما﴾, accusative by position and genitive by the bāʾ in form.
﴿شيطان﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿رجيم﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿شيطان﴾, genitive by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿فأين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and ayna is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as a vague, non-specific adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تذهبون﴾.
﴿تذهبون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿إن﴾: in is negative.
﴿هو﴾: an indeclinable (mabnī) pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿ذكر﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative.
﴿للعالمين﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ذكر﴾, or a naʿt (adjective) of it.

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿لمن﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, a badal (substitute) from His saying ﴿لـالعالمين﴾ with repetition of the governing word, which is the lām.
﴿شاء﴾: a past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿شاء﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿مَن﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿منكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle.
﴿يستقيم﴾: an imperfect verb in the subjunctive (manṣūb); an and what falls within its scope are mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿شاء﴾. The clause ﴿يستقيم﴾ is the ṣila of the particle-relative ﴿أن﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and mā is negative.
﴿تشاءون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿إلا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr).
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle.
﴿يشاء﴾: an imperfect verb in the subjunctive (manṣūb).
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; an and what follows it are in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition, and the (implied) preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تشاءون﴾.
﴿رب﴾: a badal (substitute), or a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty ﴿الله﴾.
﴿العالمين﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis ﴿علمت﴾.
﴿الشمس﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an implied (muqaddar) verb indicated by what follows it; and it was said: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause made up of the omitted verb and the nāʾib fāʿil is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿كورت﴾: a past verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause «كورت» is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis ﴿علمت﴾.
﴿النجوم﴾: fāʿil (agent) of an implied (muqaddar) verb indicated by what follows it; and it was said: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause made up of the omitted verb and the fāʿil is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿انكدرت﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿انكدرت﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿وإذا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «إذا» is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis ﴿علمت﴾.
﴿الجبال﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an implied (muqaddar) verb indicated by what follows it; and it was said: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). The clause made up of the omitted verb and the nāʾib fāʿil is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.
﴿سيرت﴾: a past verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿سيرت﴾ is explicative (tafsīriyya), with no grammatical position.

﴿ذنب﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿قتلت﴾: a past verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause stands in place of the second object of ﴿سئلت﴾.
