muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿علمت﴾: the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of «إذا»; «علمت» is a past verb, the tāʾ being for the feminine.
﴿نفس﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿ما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿أحضرت﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿أحضرت﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and «لا» is connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant).
﴿أقسم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "anā" (I).
﴿بالخنس﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقسم﴾; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿الجوار﴾: «الجواري» is a naʿt (adjective), or a badal (substitute), genitive (majrūr) by the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ that was elided for lightening.
﴿الكنس﴾: a naʿt of ﴿الجواري﴾.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿والليل﴾: the wāw is also for the oath, and «الليل» is genitive by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear" (أقسم).
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf), attached to the verb of the oath.
﴿عسعس﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿عسعس﴾ is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿والصبح﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «الصبح» is conjoined, genitive by the wāw of oath; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "I swear" (أقسم).
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb (ẓarf), attached to the verb of the oath.
﴿تنفس﴾: a past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause ﴿تنفس﴾ is in the position of a genitive, the adverb being put in construct with it.

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿إنه﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun.
﴿لقول﴾: the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and «قول» is the khabar (predicate) of ﴿إن﴾.
﴿رسول﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿كريم﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to the oath.

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿ذي﴾: «ذي» is a second adjective (ṣifa) of ﴿رسول﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ, because it is one of the six nouns.
﴿قوة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿عند﴾: an adverb of place (ẓarf makān), accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted [element], a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مكين», because it was originally an adjective of it, and when it was placed before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl.
﴿ذي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿العرش﴾: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿مكين﴾: a third adjective of ﴿رسول﴾, genitive.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t: الشّمس is nominative by an implied verb like the second [i.e. the overt one], because إِذَا is on the level of the conditional particles, followed only by a verb, overt or implied. It is related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: كُوِّرَتْ means its light went away; and from Ibn ʿAbbās: it was darkened. Abū Jaʿfar said: One says كوّر الشيء and كبّر الشيء when it is wrapped up and thrown. In the ḥadīth: «نعوذ بك من الحور بعد الكون» ("We seek refuge in You from decline after being"), i.e. from going back after our affairs were in good order; it is also related as «بعد الكور».

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: Thus [نُشِرَتْ, without doubling] read Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ and ʿĀṣim. Abū ʿAmr, Ibn Kathīr, Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read نُشِّرَتْ [with doubling], their argument being صُحُفاً مُنَشَّرَةً [al-Muddaththir: 52]. [Translator's note: the source prints both readings as «نشرت/نُشِرَتْ»; the doubling of the second is supplied from the argument given.] This is not one of the arguments that require abandoning what was read by those whose reading constitutes proof, because نشرت applies to the few and the many according to the grammarians; both readings are sound.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: Al-Farrāʾ said: [كُشِطَتْ means] removed and folded up. He said: and likewise قشطت, as you say كافور and قافور.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: [سُعِّرَتْ with doubling] is the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Nāfiʿ, and the reading of Abū ʿAmr and the Kufans is سُعِرَتْ. [Translator's note: the source prints the second reading with the doubling sign; it is supplied here according to the argument that follows.] It is argued for them that الجحيم is one; and it is argued against them that الجحيم, even though it is one, is more fitting for intensification because of the frequency of the kindling. Aḥmad ibn ʿUbayd said: one says جحمت النار, i.e. I increased its fuel. Al-Farrāʾ said: جحمت الجمر means I put the embers one on top of another, and a جاحم man is a stingy miser.

nahhas-irab:13-14.t: [الْجَنَّةُ is nominative] by an implied verb, like the second [the overt one]. The answer (jawāb) of «إذا» is عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما أَحْضَرَتْ (14). It was said: its meaning is "what it found present", as you say أحمدت فلانا, i.e. I found him praiseworthy. Qatāda said: [it means] what it brought forward of deeds.

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
«لا» is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, i.e. "I swear by الخنس". There are three views on the meaning of الخنس. Among them, what has been related from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, has been mentioned already: that they are the five stars [i.e. planets]. Saʿīd related from Simāk, who said: I heard Khālid ibn ʿArʿara say: I heard ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, say: «الخنّس» are the stars which withdraw (تخنس) by day and hide (تكنس) by night. The apparent sense of this view is general, covering all the stars; it is the view of al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, Qatāda, Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd. ʿIkrima related from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: الخنّس are the gazelles; this is the view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk. Jābir ibn Zayd and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: الخنس are the wild cows. Abū Jaʿfar said: If the implied form is "I swear by the Lord of الخنس", the meaning is one; but the first view is the most eminent and the best known of them. Wild cows and gazelles are called خنّس [because of their snub noses]; the singular is أخنس and خنساء, as the poet said: [al-kāmil] 544-
خنساء ضيّعت الغرير فلم ترم ... عرض الشّقائق طرفها ويغامها
(A snub-nosed [wild cow] who lost her young calf, and her glance and her lowing did not leave the expanse of the sand-ridges.)
The singular of الخنس [in the sense of the stars] is خانس, and the plural is خنّس and خنّاس.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: «الجواري» is in the position of the genitive; the kasra was dropped from the yāʾ because of its heaviness. If it is without alif and lām, the yāʾ is dropped because it and the nunation are both vowelless, since it is the plural of جارية; and likewise if you name [someone] with it, according to the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. As for the Kufans and Yūnus, they say: if you name a man جوار, you do not decline it as a triptote in the accusative and genitive, so you say رأيت جواري and مررت بجواري [Translator's note: the source has «بواري» in the first example, apparently a misprint for «جواري».], and in the nominative it is said هؤلاء جواري with the yāʾ vowelless. Al-Khalīl said: This is a mistake, because on this [basis] one would have to say هذا جواريُ فاعلم with ḍamma on the yāʾ. He said: It does not become heavier than فواعل when you name [someone] with it. Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about a woman named قاض, and he said: It is declined in the nominative and genitive; you say مررت بقاض and هذه قاض. Abū Jaʿfar said: The view of Yūnus and the Kufans [is]: مررت بقاضي and هذا قاضي فاعلم. الْكُنَّسِ is the plural of كانس; one also says كنّاس.

nahhas-irab:17-18.t: وَاللَّيْلِ is conjoined to «الخنس»; the wāw is not a wāw of oath. إِذا عَسْعَسَ: al-Farrāʾ said: The exegetes agreed that it means "when it advances". This is a mistake: Mujāhid related from Ibn ʿAbbās [that] «إذا عسعس» [means] "when it retreats". Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: إِذا تَنَفَّسَ means when it shines and advances.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: [إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ is] the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam). Al-Kisāʾī permitted «أنه» with fatḥa, i.e. "I swear that it…", and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd the grammarian followed him in that.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: النجوم is nominative by an implied verb as well. Ubayy said: انْكَدَرَتْ means they were scattered. Ibn ʿAbbās said: they were strewn about.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: ذِي قُوَّةٍ is a naʿt (adjective) of رسول, i.e. possessing strength in [carrying out] the command of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, and obedience to Him. عِنْدَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ مَكِينٍ is also a naʿt, i.e. possessing a high rank.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: مُطاعٍ ثَمَّ, i.e. obeyed in the heavens. أَمِينٍ: [trustworthy] over the revelation of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, and His messages. This is the complete stop (tamām).

nahhas-irab:22-22.t: That is, neither his address, nor his explanation, nor his action is the action of a madman.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: The hāʾ refers back to the messenger, who is Jibrīl ﷺ, as was read [in transmission] to Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥafṣ, from Yūsuf ibn Mūsā, from Yazīd ibn Hārūn: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind narrated to us, from al-Shaʿbī, from Masrūq, who said: I said to ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: O Mother of the Believers, Allah the Exalted says: وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالْأُفُقِ الْمُبِينِ (23). She said: I was the first to ask the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [about it], and he said: «That was Jibrīl ﷺ. I have not seen him in the form in which he was created except twice: [I saw him] descending from the heaven, the immensity of his form filling what is between the heaven and the earth.»

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: [بِضَنِينٍ with ḍād is] the reading of Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Yaḥyā, al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza, and it is said that it is likewise in the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb. Three of the Companions read «بظنين», as was read [in transmission] to Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā, from Ismāʿīl, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Madīnī, from Sufyān, from ʿAmr, who said: I heard Ibn ʿAbbās reading «بظنين» with ẓāʾ. Shuʿba related from Mughīra from Mujāhid, who said: I heard ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr reading بظنين with ẓāʾ. ʿUrwa said: I heard ʿĀʾisha reading it with ẓāʾ. It is the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī. There is no disagreement among the exegetes and lexicographers that the meaning of «بظنين» is "suspected" and «بضنين» "miserly". Both readings are sound, and the majority have transmitted them, except that in the written text (السواد) it is with ḍād. Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī, who are the two grammarians of the readers, inclined to the reading «بظنين», because one says فلان ظنين على كذا, i.e. suspected concerning it, and ظنين بكذا — even though with the genitive-governing particles something like this is easily [interchanged]. Abū ʿUbayd also inclined to it, because he mentioned that it is an answer, since they had called him a liar. This which he argued from — we know of no one among the people of knowledge who recognises it or considers it to be an answer; in their view it is nothing but a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). We have said that both readings are sound. The sense of «ضنين» is that some scholars are miserly with their knowledge, and in the ḥadīth: «من كتم علما لجمه الله بلجام من نار» ("Whoever conceals knowledge, Allah will bridle him with a bridle of fire"). So Allah has informed about His Prophet ﷺ that he is not miserly with anything of the matter of religion, and that he did not reserve it for one person rather than another — contrary to what some people say, that he reserved for the Imām what he did not convey to anyone else.

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: If the bāʾ were omitted, you would put [it] in the accusative because of the resemblance of «ما» to ليس.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t:
Al-Farrāʾ mentioned ] [Translator's note: a stray bracket appears here in the source.] that the meaning is "to where are you going", with «إلى» omitted, as one says ذهبت الشام and ذهبت إلى الشام ("I went to Syria"), انطلقت إلى السوق and انطلقت السّوق ("I set off to the market"), خرجت الشام and إلى الشام. Al-Kisāʾī reported انطلق به الغور ("he was taken off to the lowland"); the implied form in his view is "to الغور", with «إلى» omitted. So the Kufans made these three verbs — انطلق, ذهب and خرج — ones with which the omission of إلى is permissible, and they drew analogies from what they heard of that, so they claimed. As for Sībawayh, he reported one of them only and does not permit any other, namely ذهبت الشام; he does not permit ذهبت مصر. On this is the view of the Basrans: they do not draw analogy from any of this.
Abū al-ʿAbbās related something on this, claiming that their saying ذهبت الشام has the sense of vagueness, i.e. "I went towards the left side (شامة) of the Kaʿba". However, this can only be referred back to the word of those who reported it from the Arabs, and Sībawayh reported it only as meaning Syria itself.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: That is, there is nothing in the Qur'an but admonition and reminder for the worlds.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t: لِمَنْ is a badal (substitute) for العالمين with repetition of the lām; had it been without the lām it would have been permissible. Mujāhid said: لِمَنْ شاءَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ (28), i.e. to follow the truth.

nahhas-irab:29-29.t: وَما تَشاؤُنَ: there are two views on its meaning. One of them: "you do not will to be upright", i.e. to follow the truth, إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ. The other view is that it is [general] about them, i.e. "you do not will anything of obedience or disobedience إِلَّا أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعالَمِينَ that from you"; and had He not willed, He would have come between you and it. [Translator's note: «ما تشاؤون يشاء» in the source appears garbled; rendered according to the evident sense.]

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: [الْجِبالُ is nominative] by an implied verb as well.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: عُطِّلَتْ: he said: i.e. neglected. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: العشراء is the she-camel when ten months of her pregnancy have passed. Abū ʿUbayda said: [it is] the she-camel from when six months of her pregnancy have passed until she gives birth, and after that; they keep checking on her and she is precious to them.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: There are two views about it. One of them: they will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection so that Allah may compensate them for the pain that befell them in this world. Qatāda said: حشرت means they were brought together.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t:
Abū ʿAmr read سُجِرَتْ ] [Translator's note: a stray bracket appears here in the source, which also prints the word with the doubling sign.] without doubling (mukhaffaf), and argued from الْبَحْرِ الْمَسْجُورِ. A group of the people of knowledge among the lexicographers disagreed with him, saying: البحر المسجور is singular, while البحار is a plural of plural, more fitting for intensification and doubling. They said: البحر المسجور is a sea whose description is this, and it is not like وَإِذَا الْبِحارُ سُجِّرَتْ. Abū Jaʿfar said: We have mentioned its meaning; it is well known in the language that one says سجرت الشيء meaning "I filled it", as the poet said: [al-kāmil] 541-
فتوسّطا عرض السّريّ وصدّعا ... مسجورة متجاورا قلّامها
(The two went into the middle of the stream and parted a full [spring] whose reeds were close together.)
And he said: [al-mutaqārib] 542-
إذا شاء طالع مسجورة ... يرى حولها النّبع والسّاسما
(When he wishes he looks out over a full [pool], around which he sees nabʿ and sāsam trees.)
That is, filled. It was also said: these are seas in Hell, when the Day of Resurrection comes; سجّرت means they were filled with kinds of punishment. However, Abū al-ʿĀliya said: [From] إذا الشمس كوّرت to six of them [are signs] that people will see before the Resurrection takes place, and six are in the Hereafter after the Resurrection takes place. He said: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb narrated to me, saying: While people are in their markets, the light of the sun goes away; while they are in that state, the stars are scattered; while they are in that state, the mountains fall and the earth quakes, and the jinn flee to humans and humans to the jinn; the pregnant camels are neglected, i.e. their owners neglect them; and the wild beasts mingle with people — that is their gathering. The jinn say to the humans: We will find out the news for you. So they go to the seas and find that they have been kindled into fires. Then the earth splits open down to the lowest earth [and] up to the highest heaven, then the wind is sent upon them and kills them.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t:
That is, the righteous is brought close [paired] with the righteous; this is the meaning of the saying of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him. وَإِذَا الْمَوْؤُدَةُ سُئِلَتْ (8): one says وأدها يئدها وأدا, so he is وائد and she is موءودة, when he buried her alive and threw earth over her. Its derivation is from وأده, when he weighed him down. Hārūn the Reciter said: in the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy it is وَإِذَا الْمَوْؤُدَةُ سَأَلَتْ. [Translator's note: the source prints this as «سُئِلَتْ», identical to the canonical text; the variant attributed to Ubayy is «سألت» ("asked"), as the following discussion shows.] Abū ʿUbayd said: This is clearer in meaning. Abū Jaʿfar said: He was contradicted in this, because it is an irregular (shādhdh) reading that differs from the Muṣḥaf and is problematic, because the implied form could be "she asked her Lord, Majestic and Mighty is He" or "she asked her killer". This is an obscure meaning, so how can it be clear? There are two views on the meaning of سئلت:
One of them is that the meaning is that she is asked who killed her, as a rebuke to him; she is told: Who killed you? The other meaning is that she is asked, being told: Why were you killed without a sin? — as a rebuke to her killer, just as ʿĪsā ﷺ will be told: "Did you say to people: Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?" Al-Farrāʾ claimed that like this is the poet's saying: [al-kāmil] 543-
الشّاتمي عرضي ولم أشتمهما ... والناذرين إذا لم القهما دمي
(The two who revile my honour though I have not reviled them, and who vow my blood when I have not met them.)
The meaning is not that they did this when they met him; rather, the meaning is "and the two who vow, saying: when we meet him we will kill him". It is soundly established from Ibn ʿAbbās that he inferred from this verse that all children are in Paradise; he said: because Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has taken their side against those who wronged them. [And] he ﷺ said: «الله أعلم بما كانوا عاملين» ("Allah knows best what they would have done").

safi-cedvel:1-14.t:
* I'rab:
(إذا) is an adverb of the future, in the position of an accusative, attached to the apodosis علمت, and likewise the remaining conjoined adverbs; (الشمس) is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb that what follows explains, its implied form being انطوت, and the nouns after the following adverbs are parsed likewise; (الجبال) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being انتثرت; (العشار) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being سرحت وحدها; (الوحوش) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being اجتمعت; (البحار) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being اختلطت or امتلأت; (النفوس) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being اقترنت; (الموؤدة) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being تظلّمت; (بأيّ) is attached to (قتلت) and (الباء) is causal; (الصحف) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being ظهرت; (السماء) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being زالت; (الجحيم) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being اشتعلت; (الجنّة) is the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being قربت [Note: Some exegetes, however, permitted parsing each of the mentioned nouns as a nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb of the passive type that comes after it ...] , (ما) is a relative noun in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the returning pronoun is omitted..
Clause: « (انطوت) الشمس ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi ... and the clause of the condition, its verb and its apodosis.. has no grammatical position, inceptive.
And the clause: «كوّرت ... » has no grammatical position, explicative.
And the clauses: «the condition, its verb and its apodosis, the following eleven ... » have no grammatical position, conjoined to the inceptive.
And the clauses: «the ones implied after (إذا) ... » are in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clauses: «the ones mentioned in the passive ... » have no grammatical position, explicative.
And the clause: «قتلت ... » is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi of the verb of asking that is suspended by the interrogative, with the preposition عن implied.
And the clause: «علمت نفس ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
And the clause: «أحضرت ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما) .

* Morphology:
(4) العشار: plural of عشراء, a noun for a pregnant she-camel, on the pattern فعلاء (with ḍamma, then fatḥa); the plural is فعال (with kasra on the fāʾ).
(5) الوحوش: plural of وحش, a noun for a beast of the earth, on the pattern فعل (with fatḥa then sukūn); the plural is فعول (with ḍamma on the fāʾ).
(8) الموؤدة: a noun for the girl who is buried alive; it is a passive participle of the triliteral وأد, on the pattern مفعول.

* Rhetoric:
Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His saying, the Exalted, «عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما أَحْضَرَتْ» .
The indefiniteness of النفس conveys that the stated knowledge holds for one individual among souls, or for some of them, to signal that its holding for all individuals without exception is so manifest and clear that not even a trace of doubt hovers around it at all, and everyone knows it; thus this indefiniteness gives generality.

safi-cedvel:15-22.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (لا) redundant (zāʾida); (بالخنّس) attached to (أقسم); (الجوار) is a badal (substitute) for الخنّس, genitive, with the genitive sign being the implied kasra on the omitted yāʾ because of the reading in connected speech (waṣl); (الكنّس) is a genitive naʿt (adjective) of الجواري; (الواو) is a conjunction in the two places; (الليل) is conjoined to الخنّس, genitive; (إذا) is an adverb in the position of an accusative, stripped of the conditional sense, attached to (أقسم); (الصبح إذا تنفّس) is like الليل إذا عسعس; (اللام) in the position of the lām of oath, for emphasis, a substitute for the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); (ذي) is a genitive naʿt of رسول; (عند) is an accusative adverb of time, attached to (مكين) [Note: or to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of مكين.] and it is a genitive naʿt of رسول; (ثمّ) is an adverb indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative, attached to (مطاع); (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما) is a negative working like ليس; (مجنون) is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما.
Clause: «أقسم ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «عسعس ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «تنفّس ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «إنّه لقول ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the oath.
And the clause: «ما صاحبكم بمجنون ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(15) الخنّس: plural of خانس, an active participle of the triliteral خنس (of the bāb of نصر) meaning "to withdraw and draw back"; it is a name for the planets other than the moon, on the pattern فاعل; the plural is فعّل (with ḍamma on the fāʾ and a doubled fatḥa-vowelled ʿayn).
(16) الكنّس: its derivation is like that of الخنّس and its meaning the same, from the triliteral كنس (of the bāb of ضرب) meaning "to disappear into its place".
(21) مطاع: a passive participle of the quadriliteral أطاع, on the pattern مفعل (with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn); it has an ʿilāl (weak-letter change) by substitution, its origin being مطوع: the ṭāʾ was vowelled with fatḥa by transferring the vowel of the wāw, then the wāw was turned into alif because what precedes it has a fatḥa.

* Rhetoric:
Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَالصُّبْحِ إِذا تَنَفَّسَ» .
Since breath is a particular wind that relieves the heart, through expansion and contraction, that breeze was likened to breath, and the name of the borrowed term was applied to it. The dawn was made a breather because of its accompanying it. It is also possible that, after the metaphor, it is a kināya (allusion) to illumination. It is also possible that here there is an implicit metaphor (makniyya) with an imaginative attribute (takhyīliyya), by likening the dawn to one who walks and comes from a far distance, and affirming for it breathing, by which is meant the blowing of its breeze, figuratively by way of imagination.

safi-cedvel:23-26.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) is a conjunction; (اللام) is the lām of oath; (قد) is a particle of certainty; (بالأفق) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ in (رآه) [Note: or attached to (رآه), the باء being locative.] .
And the clause: «قد رآه ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما صاحبكم بمجنون [Note: in the preceding verse (22) .] .
24- (الواو) is a conjunction, or circumstantial; (ما) is a negative working like ليس; (هو), i.e. the Messenger, peace be upon him; (على الغيب) is attached to (ضنين); (ضنين) is genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of ما.
And the clause: «ما هو ... بضنين» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause رآه [Note: the clause may be in the position of an accusative ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) of رآه.] .
25- (الواو) is a conjunction; (ما هو بقول) is like ما هو بضنين, and the pronoun of the absent third person refers to the Noble Qur'an.
And the clause: «ما هو بقول ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause ما هو بضنين.
26- (الفاء) connects the apodosis of an omitted conditional; (أين) is an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative, an adverb of place attached to (تذهبون) with the preposition إلى implied.
And the clause: «تذهبون ... » is in the position of a jussive, the apodosis of an omitted conditional, i.e.: if the matter of Muḥammad and the Qur'an has become clear to you, then where are you going ...

* Morphology:
(24) ضنين: a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from the triliteral ضنّ (of the bāb of ضرب) meaning "to be stingy with something", on the pattern فعيل.

* Benefits:
- The parsing of conditional and interrogative nouns and the like: all of them are indeclinable, except (أي), which is declinable. Their position in parsing: if a preposition or a muḍāf precedes them, their position is genitive, as in His saying, the Exalted, (عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ) and our saying (صبيحة أيّ يوم سفرك؟) and (غلام من جاءك؟) .
If it refers to time, it is an adverb of time, as in His saying, the Exalted, (أَيَّانَ يُبْعَثُونَ) ; or to place, it is in the position of an accusative as an adverb of place, as in His saying, the Exalted: (فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ) ; or to an event, it is the deputy of a mafʿūl muṭlaq, as in His saying, the Exalted, (وَسَيَعْلَمُ الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا أَيَّ مُنْقَلَبٍ يَنْقَلِبُونَ) . If an indefinite noun follows it, as in (من أب لك؟) , it is a mubtadaʾ; or a definite noun, as in (من أبوك) , it is a khabar or a mubtadaʾ. These two kinds do not occur with conditional nouns because the latter are specific to verbs. Otherwise, if an intransitive verb follows it, it is a mubtadaʾ, as in (من قام) and (من يقم أقم معه) , and the sounder view, as Ibn Hishām says, is that the khabar is the verb of the protasis, not the verb of the apodosis; some hold that the verbs of the protasis and the apodosis together are the khabar. If a transitive verb follows it, then if the verb falls upon it, it is a mafʿūl bihi, as in His saying, the Exalted (أَيَّ آياتِ اللَّهِ تُنْكِرُونَ)
and (أَيًّا ما تَدْعُوا فَلَهُ الْأَسْماءُ الْحُسْنى) and (مَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَلا هادِيَ لَهُ) ; but if the verb falls upon its pronoun, as in (من رأيته) , or on something related to it, as in (من رأيت أخاه؟) , then it is a mubtadaʾ, or accusative by an omitted implied verb after it that the mentioned one explains.
- Note:
When the conditional noun is a mubtadaʾ, is its khabar the verb of the protasis alone, because it is a complete noun and the protasis verb contains its pronoun (for if (من يقم) had no conditional sense it would be equivalent to your saying (كل من الناس يقوم) )? Or the verb of the apodosis, because the benefit is completed by it, and because they require a pronoun to return from it to it, on the sounder view, and because its counterpart is the khabar in your saying (الذي يأتيني فله درهم) ? Or both together, because your saying (من يقم أقم معه) is equivalent to your saying «كل من الناس إن يقم أقم معه» ? The correct view is the first; the completion of the benefit depends on the apodosis only in terms of connection, not in terms of being a khabar. This is what Ibn Hishām reported in al-Mughnī.

safi-cedvel:27-29.t:
* I'rab:
(إن) is a particle of negation; (إلّا) is for restriction; (لمن) is a badal (substitute) for العالمين with repetition of the preposition; (منكم) is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of شاء; (أن) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle that puts the verb in the accusative; (الواو) is resumptive; (ما) is a negative; (إلّا) is for restriction; (أن) is a maṣdar particle that puts the verb in the accusative; (ربّ) is a naʿt (adjective) of the divine name.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يستقيم) is in the position of an accusative, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يشاء..) is in the position of a genitive by an omitted preposition, namely الباء, attached to (تشاؤون) [Note: the maṣdar may be in the position of an accusative as an adverbial, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e.: "except at the time of Allah's willing.."; and the object of (تشاؤون) , and of (يشاء الله) , is omitted, its implied form being "uprightness upon the truth".] .
Clause: «إن هو إلّا ذكر ... » has no grammatical position, causal for the content of the preceding negation.
And the clause: «شاء ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من) .
And the clause: «يستقيم ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن) .
And the clause: «ما تشاؤون ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يشاء الله ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-relative (أن) .

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {إِذَا الشمس}: There are two aspects to the nominative of «الشمسِ». The more correct is that it is nominative by an implied passive verb, deleted and explained by what follows, by way of ishtighāl (preoccupation of the verb). The nominative on this aspect—I mean with the verb implied—is obligatory according to the Basrans, because they do not allow anything else to follow it [i.e. «إذا»], and they reinterpret whatever gives an impression to the contrary. The second: that it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); this is the view of the Kufans and al-Akhfash, on the basis of instances that have occurred in poetry; Ibn Mālik supported it, and there I set out the discussion with him. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The nominative of «الشمس» is as a mubtadaʾ or as an agent. I say: rather, as an agent"; then he mentioned something like what has preceded. By "as an agent" he means its being nominative by a verb in the clause; it has passed that the object of a verb whose agent is not named is called an agent. The explanation of al-takwīr has preceded at the beginning of «تنزيلُ» «[Translator's note: so in the text]». The nominative of «النجوم» and what follows it is as has preceded for «الشمس».

semin-durr:2-2.t:
Al-inkidār is scattering, i.e. they plunged down as the eagle plunges down when it swoops. Al-ʿAjjāj said, describing a falcon:
4510 - أَبْصَرَ خِرْبانَ الفَلاةِ فانكَدَرْ ... تَقَضِّيَ البازيْ إذا البازيْ كَسَرْ
(It saw the bustards of the desert and plunged down, with the swoop of the falcon when the falcon folds its wings.)

semin-durr:4-4.t:
Al-ʿishār is the plural of ʿusharāʾ, the she-camel ten months of whose pregnancy have passed; that remains her name until she gives birth at the completion of the year. Likewise «نِفاس» as the plural of nufasāʾ. It was also said: al-ʿishār are the clouds, and «عُطِّلت» means they do not rain. It was also said: the land whose cultivation has been left idle. Al-taʿṭīl is neglecting; from it a woman is called ʿāṭil when she has no jewellery on her. It has preceded / at «بئرٍ مُعَطَّلةٍ». Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4511 - وجِيْدٍ كجِيْدِ الرِّئْمِ ليس بفاحشٍ ... إذا هي نَصَّتْهُ ولا بمُعَطَّلِ
(And a neck like the neck of the white gazelle, not ungainly when she raises it, nor bare of ornament.)
Ibn Kathīr, in one transmission, read «عُطِلت» with the ṭāʾ undoubled. Al-Rāzī said: "It is a mistake; it is only «عَطَلَتْ» with two fatḥas, meaning taʿaṭṭalat (became idle), because the doubling in it is for transitivity. One says: ʿaṭṭaltu the thing and aʿṭaltuhu, so it ʿaṭala."
Al-wuḥūsh are the land animals that have not become tame. Al-waḥsh is also the place in which there is no human company; from it: I met him in the desolate land of Iṣmit, i.e. in a deserted country. Al-waḥsh is also the one whose stomach passes the night empty of food, its plural being awḥāsh. What is related to a desolate place is called waḥshī. Al-waḥshī is used to express the side opposite to the insī, the insī being the side that faces a person; on this basis are the waḥshī and the insī [sides] of the horse. Al-Ḥasan and Ibn Maymūn read «حُشِّرَتْ» with doubling of the shīn.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {سُجِّرَتْ}: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «سُجِرَتْ» with the jīm undoubled, and the rest with it doubled, for intensity and multiplicity. The derivation of this root has preceded.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {زُوِّجَتْ}: The majority read it with doubling of the wāw, from al-tazwīj (pairing). It is related from ʿĀṣim «زُوْوِجَتْ» on the pattern fūʿilat. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "And al-mufāʿala is between two parties." End of quotation. I say: it is a problematic reading, because it would have to be pronounced with a quiescent wāw followed by another with kasra; and it has preceded for you that when two identical letters meet and the first of them is quiescent, assimilation is obligatory even across two words, so within a single word all the more so.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {الموءودة}: She is the girl buried alive, from al-waʾd, which is weighing down, because she is weighed down with earth and stones. One says waʾadahu yaʾiduhu, like waʿadahu yaʿiduhu. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Waʾada yaʾidu is a metathesis of āda yaʾūdu, when it weighs down. Allah the Exalted said: {وَلاَ يَؤُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا} [al-Baqara: 255]; because it is a weighing down with earth." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "That cannot be claimed, because each of them is fully inflected in the past, the imperative, the imperfect, the maṣdar (verbal noun), the active participle and the passive participle, and there is nothing in it of what justifies claiming metathesis. What shows the original as against the metathesised is: that one of the two arrangements has a rule in it testifying to its originality while the other does not; or its being free of augment letters while the other contains an augment; or its being more fully inflected while the other is not; or its being more used than the other—this according to what has been established and made firm in the science of morphology (taṣrīf). The first is like yaʾisa and ayisa; the second like ṭaʾmana and iṭmaʾanna; the third like shawāyiʿ and shawāʿī; and the fourth like laʿamrī and raʿamlī."
The majority read «المَوْءُوْدَة» with a hamza between two quiescent wāws, like al-mawʿūda. Al-Bazzī, in one transmission, read it with a hamza with ḍamma and then a quiescent wāw. There are two aspects to it. The first: that it is like the reading of the group; then the vowel of the hamza was transferred to the wāw before it and the hamza was deleted, so the word became al-mawūda: a wāw with ḍamma followed by another, quiescent one; then the wāw with ḍamma was changed into a hamza, as in «أُجوه» for wujūh, and the word became as you see. Its pattern is now al-mafūla, because what was deleted is the middle radical. The second: that the word is a passive participle of ādahu yaʾūduhu, like qādahu yaqūduhu. The origin is maʾwūda, like maqwūda; then one of the two wāws was deleted, according to the well-known disagreement on the deletion in forms such as maqūl and maṣūn. Its pattern is now either mafuʿla, if we say that what was deleted is the augment wāw, or mafūla, if we say that what was deleted is the middle radical. This shows the merit of the science of morphology.
It has been read «المَوُوْدة» with ḍamma on the first wāw, on the basis that he transferred the vowel of the hamza after deleting it and did not change the wāw into a hamza. Al-Aʿmash read «المَوْدَة» on the pattern of al-mawza. Its justification is that he deleted the hamza arbitrarily, so two quiescent letters met and he deleted the second of them; its pattern is al-mafla, because the hamza is the middle radical and it has been deleted. Makkī said: "Rather, it is a regular lightening; that is, when he transferred the vowel of the hamza to the wāw he did not give it a hamza, then found the ḍamma on it heavy and made it quiescent; so two quiescent letters met and he deleted the second." All of this is a departure from the apparent. What appears in this is only what the readers transmitted about Ḥamza's pausal form: that he pauses on it like al-mawza. They said: because of the script, since it was written thus, and the script is a sunna to be followed.
The majority read «سُئِلت» in the passive with ḍamma on the sīn; al-Ḥasan read it with kasra, from sāla yasālu, as has preceded. Abū Jaʿfar read «قُتِّلَتْ» with doubling of the tāʾ, for multiplicity, because what is meant is the genus noun, so multiplicity suits it.
ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd «[Translator's note: the text has «معسود», a misprint for «مسعود»]» and Ibn ʿAbbās read «سَأَلَتْ» in the active, and «قُتِلْتُ» with ḍamma on the final tāʾ, which is that of the first person, as a report of her own words. From Ubayy, Ibn Masʿūd also, and Ibn Yaʿmar: «سَأَلَتْ» in the active, and «قُتِلَتْ» with the quiescent tāʾ of the feminine, like the reading of the majority.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {نُشِرَتْ}: The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī], Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read it with doubling, and the rest without doubling. Nāfiʿ, Ḥafṣ and Ibn Dhakwān / read «سُعِّرَتْ» with doubling, and the rest without doubling.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {عَلِمَتْ}: This is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إذا» at the beginning of the sūra and of what is conjoined to it.
His saying: {كُشِطَتْ} [al-Takwīr: 11]: i.e. stripped off, from their saying: kashaṭa the skin of the sheep, i.e. flayed it. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read «قُشِطَتْ» with qāf. It has preceded that the two often alternate, and that «قافوراً» and «كافوراً» have been read in {هَلْ أتى عَلَى الإنسان}.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {بالخنس}: the plural of khānis; al-khunūs is withdrawing. One says khanasa from the people and inkhanasa. In the ḥadīth: "So I inkhanastu", i.e. I slipped away and hid. Al-khanas is the receding of the nose from the lip with the tip slightly raised; one says an akhnas man and a khansāʾ woman; from it is al-Khansāʾ the poetess. Al-khunnas in the Qur'an: it was said they are seven stars: the sun and moon (al-qamarān), Saturn, Venus, Jupiter, Mars and Mercury. Al-kunnas are those entering al-kinās, which is the lair of wild animals. Al-jawārī is the plural of jāriya (running). It was also said: they are the wild cows, because this is their description. It was also said: the gazelles; they said: because snub-nosedness (al-khanas) is found in them.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {عَسْعَسَ}: One says ʿasʿasa and saʿsaʿa: it approached. Al-ʿAjjāj said:
4512 - حتى إذا الصُّبْحُ لها تَنَفَّسا ... وانْجابَ عنها ليلُها وعَسْعَسا
(Until, when the morning breathed for her, and her night was cleared from her and departed.)
i.e. departed. It was also said: it has both meanings by way of homonymy. It was also said: it means "departed" in the dialect of Quraysh specifically. It was also said: its darkness approached; this is supported by its being contrasted with His saying {والصبح إِذَا تَنَفَّسَ}, and this is close to its departing.

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {عِندَ ذِي العرش}: It may be a naʿt (adjective) of «رسولٍ», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «مَكين»; its origin is being an adjective [of it], and when it was put before it, it became accusative as a ḥāl.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {ثَمَّ أَمِينٍ}: The majority read it with fatḥa on the thāʾ, because it is an adverb of place for what is far, and what governs it is «مُطاعٍ». Abū al-Barahsam, Abū Jaʿfar and Abū Ḥaywa read it with ḍamma [«ثُمَّ»], making it a conjunction; the sequence here is in rank, because the second [quality] is greater than the first.

semin-durr:24-24.t: His saying: {بِضَنِينٍ}: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read it with ẓāʾ [«بظنين»], meaning "suspected", from ẓanna in the sense of "suspected", so it takes one object. It was also said: its meaning is weak in power to convey [the message], from their saying "a ẓanūn well", i.e. one with little water. It is thus in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd]. The rest read it with ḍād, meaning: miserly with what comes to him from his Lord. However, al-Ṭabarī transmitted that the ḍād is the script of all the codices, and that is not so, for the reason that has passed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to read it thus «[Translator's note: the text does not specify which of the two letters is meant here]». This is evidence of the distinction between the two letters, contrary to those who say that if one of them occurred in place of the other it would be permissible, because of the difficulty of knowing it. Al-Zamakhsharī censured those who say that, and mentioned some of the points of articulation and some of the attributes, in a way that it is not fitting to discuss at length. «على الغيب» is attached to «ظَنِين» or to «بضَنِين».

semin-durr:26-26.t: His saying: {فَأيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ}: «أين» is accusative by «تَذْهبون», because it is a vague (mubham) adverb. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "I.e. to where; the preposition was deleted, as you say: I went [to] Syria. It may also be construed according to the meaning, as though He said: where are you heading?" «[Translator's note: the text has «تؤمنون» (believe), evidently for «تَؤُمُّون» (head for)]». He means that it is by deletion or by implication of another meaning (taḍmīn). Makkī also inclined to this. There is no need at all for that, because it is a vague adverb of place, not a specific one.

semin-durr:28-28.t: His saying: {لِمَن شَآءَ}: a badal (substitute) for «العالمين» with repetition of the governing particle. On this view His saying «أن يَسْتقيمَ» is the object of «شاء», i.e. for whoever wills uprightness. «لمَنْ شاء» may also be a fronted khabar (predicate), the object of «شاء» being omitted, and «أَنْ يَسْتَقيم» the mubtadaʾ (subject). A parallel to it has passed.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ الله رَبُّ العالمين}: i.e. except at the time of Allah's willing. Makkī said: "«أنْ» is in the position of the genitive by an implied bāʾ, or in the position of the accusative by removal of the preposition." He means that the origin is "except by [Allah's] willing" (إلاَّ بأَنْ), and in that case it [the bāʾ] is for accompaniment.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِذَا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ (١)).
The words of the Exalted (إِذَا الشَّمْسُ): i.e. «إِذَا كُوِّرَتِ الشَّمْسُ» (when the sun is wrapped up), and the apodosis (jawāb) of «إِذَا» is (عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ).

ukberi-tibyan:15-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ (١٥) الْجَوَارِ الْكُنَّسِ (١٦)).
(الْجَوَارِي) is a naʿt (adjective) of «الْخُنَّس».

ukberi-tibyan:19-21.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ (١٩) ذِي قُوَّةٍ عِنْدَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ مَكِينٍ (٢٠) مُطَاعٍ ثَمَّ أَمِينٍ (٢١)).
The words of the Exalted (عِنْدَ ذِي الْعَرْشِ): it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «رَسُولٍ», or a naʿt of «مَكِينٍ». (ثَمَّ) is governed by «مُطَاعٍ». It has also been read with a ḍamma on the thāʾ (ثُمَّ).

ukberi-tibyan:23-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالْأُفُقِ الْمُبِينِ (٢٣) وَمَا هُوَ عَلَى الْغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ (٢٤)).
The hāʾ in «رَآهُ» refers to Jibrīl, peace be upon him.
(بِظَنِينٍ) with a ẓāʾ means "suspected"; and with a ḍād (بِضَنِينٍ) means "miserly". «عَلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it on both views.

ukberi-tibyan:26-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ (٢٦) إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعَالَمِينَ (٢٧) لِمَنْ شَاءَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ (٢٨) وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٢٩)).
The words of the Exalted (فَأَيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ): i.e. «إِلَى أَيْنَ» (to where); the preposition was omitted, as they said «ذَهَبْتُ الشَّامَ» (I went to Syria). It may also be construed according to the meaning, as though He said: «أَيْنَ تُؤْمِنُونَ». [Translator's note: the text reads «تؤمنون» (you believe); the sense of construing «تذهبون» by meaning suggests «تَؤُمُّونَ» (you head for) may be intended.]
(لِمَنْ شَاءَ) is a badal (substitute) with repetition of the preposition. (إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ): i.e. except at the time of His will. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Takwīr
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿إذا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾: the meaning of ﴿كُوِّرَتْ﴾ is: its light was gathered together and wound up, as the turban is wound. One says «كُرْتُ العِمامَةَ عَلى رَأْسِي، أكُورُها» and «كَوَّرْتُها أُكَوِّرُها» when I wind it.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿وَإذا النُّجُومُ انْكَدَرَتْ﴾: «اِنْكَدَرَتْ» means they fell one after another and were scattered.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿وَإذا الجِبالُ سُيِّرَتْ﴾: they became a mirage.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿وَإذا العِشارُ عُطِّلَتْ﴾: «اَلْعِشارُ» are the pregnant she-camels that have their young in their bellies; the singular is «عُشَراءُ». They are called «عِشارٌ» only because when ten months have passed over her — and she gives birth, when she gives birth at full term, in a year — she is an عُشَراء, the finest she can be in pregnancy; and her owners do not neglect her except in the situation of the Resurrection. The Arabs were addressed with the matter of the ʿishār because their wealth and livelihood were mostly from camels.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
﴿وَإذا الوُحُوشُ حُشِرَتْ﴾: it was said: "The wild beasts will all be gathered, even the flies; they will be gathered for retaliation."
﴿وَإذا البِحارُ سُجِّرَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 6], with doubling, and it is also read «سُجِرَتْ» without doubling. As for the meaning of «سُجِّرَتْ», it was said that it is in the sense of «فُجِّرَتْ» (burst forth). It was also said: «سُجِّرَتْ» means filled; and from it is «اَلْبَحْرُ المَسْجُورُ», the filled sea. And it was said: the meaning of «سُجِّرَتْ» is: their waters were made into fires with which the people of the Fire are punished.

zajjaj:7-7.t: ﴿وَإذا النُّفُوسُ زُوِّجَتْ﴾: every faction was paired with those it followed. It was also said: they were paired with their deeds; and it was said: the bodies were paired with the souls.

zajjaj:8-9.t:
﴿وَإذا المَوْءُودَةُ سُئِلَتْ﴾ ﴿بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ﴾ — it is also read «وَإذا المَوْؤُودَةُ سَألَتْ بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ» ("and when the girl buried alive asks for what sin she was killed"). «اَلْمَوْؤُودَةُ» is the one whom the Arabs used to bury alive: when a daughter was born to one of them, he buried her alive. The meaning of her being asked "For what sin was she killed?!" is to reproach (tabkīt) her killer on the Day of Resurrection, because her answer is: "I was killed without any sin." Like this reproach is Allah the Exalted's saying: ﴿يا عِيسى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ أأنْتَ قُلْتَ لِلنّاسِ اتَّخِذُونِي وأُمِّيَ إلَهَيْنِ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ قالَ سُبْحانَكَ ما يَكُونُ لِي أنْ أقُولَ ما لَيْسَ لِي بِحَقٍّ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 116]: the question to him and his answer are only a reproach to those who claimed this about him. One says «وَأدْتُ، أئِدُ، وأْدًا» when I bury the newborn alive; the agent is «وائِدٌ», the feminine agent «وائِدَةٌ», and the feminine plural «وائِداتٌ». Al-Farazdaq said:
؎وَمِنّا الَّذِي مَنَعَ الوائِدا ∗∗∗ تِ فَأحْيا الوَئِيدَ ولَمْ يُوأدِ
(And among us is he who stopped the women who buried girls alive, so he gave life to the one to be buried, and she was not buried.)
Likewise, for whoever read «سَألَتْ بِأيِّ ذَنْبٍ قُتِلَتْ», her asking is a reproach to her killer.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَإذا الصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ﴾, and «نَشَرَتْ» (also read): the scrolls are spread open, and every person is given his book in his right hand or in his left, according to his deeds.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿وَإذا السَّماءُ كُشِطَتْ﴾ — it was also read «قُشِطَتْ» with qāf — and the meaning of both is "stripped off", as a roof is stripped off. One says «كَشَطْتُ السَّقْفَ» and «قَشَطْتُ السَّقْفَ» with one meaning. Qāf and kāf are frequently substituted one for the other; like that is «لَبَكْتُ الشَّيْءَ» and «لَبَقْتُهُ» when I mix it.

zajjaj:12-12.t: ﴿وَإذا الجَحِيمُ سُعِّرَتْ﴾ and «سُعِرَتْ», with doubling and without; its meaning is "kindled", and likewise ﴿سُعِّرَتْ﴾, except that ﴿سُعِّرَتْ﴾ means "kindled time after time".

zajjaj:13-13.t: ﴿وَإذا الجَنَّةُ أُزْلِفَتْ﴾, that is: it was brought near to the God-fearing. The answer to these things is His saying: ﴿عَلِمَتْ نَفْسٌ ما أحْضَرَتْ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 14], that is: when these things which belong to the Day of Resurrection come about, at that time every soul will know what it has brought — that is, of deeds — and will be rewarded according to its deeds.

zajjaj:15-16.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالخُنَّسِ﴾ ﴿الجَوارِ الكُنَّسِ﴾: «اَلْخُنَّسُ» is the plural of «خانِسٌ», and «اَلْجَوارِي» is the plural of «جارِيَةٌ», from «جَرى، يَجْرِي» (to run). «اَلْخُنَّسُ» is the plural of «خانِسٌ» and «خانِسَةٌ», and likewise «اَلْكُنَّسُ» is the plural of «كانِسٌ» and «كانِسَةٌ». The meaning is "So I swear", and «لا» is emphatic. As for «اَلْخُنَّسُ» here, most of the exegesis says the stars are meant by it, because they recede (takhnis), that is, disappear, because the meaning of ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا عَسْعَسَ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 17] ﴿والصُّبْحِ إذا تَنَفَّسَ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 18]…
«[Translator's note: the sentence beginning "because the meaning of…" breaks off in the source without completion.]»
The meaning of «اَلْخُنَّسُ» and «اَلْكُنَّسُ» with regard to the stars is that they rise running, and likewise recede, that is, disappear, and likewise they «تَكْنُسُ»: they enter their lair (kinās), that is, they disappear in the places where they disappear. It was also said: «اَلْخُنَّسُ» here means the wild cows and the wild gazelles. «خُنَّسٌ» is the plural of «خانِسٌ»: gazelles are khunnas and cows are khunnas; «اَلْخَنْسُ» is shortness of the nose and its lying back from the mouth. If it refers to the cows or to the gazelles, then the meaning of «اَلْكُنَّسُ» is: those that «تَكْنُسُ», that is, enter the kinās, which is a branch of the branches of trees.

zajjaj:17-17.t: ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذا عَسْعَسَ﴾: one says «عَسْعَسَ اللَّيْلُ» when the night approaches, and «عَسْعَسَ» when it departs. The two meanings come back to one thing, namely the beginning of darkness at its start and its departure at its end.

zajjaj:18-18.t: ﴿والصُّبْحِ إذا تَنَفَّسَ﴾: when it extends until it becomes clear daylight. The answer to the oath in these things — I mean ﴿فَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالخُنَّسِ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 15] and what follows it — is His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 19], meaning that the Qur'an was brought down by Jibrīl, upon him be peace.

zajjaj:20-20.t: ﴿ذِي قُوَّةٍ عِنْدَ ذِي العَرْشِ مَكِينٍ﴾: it was said that part of the strength of Jibrīl ﷺ is that he overturned the city of the people of Lūṭ with the front feathers of his wing, and they were four towns.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
﴿وَما صاحِبُكم بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾: this too is an answer to the oath. The meaning is: "So I swear by these things that the Qur'an was brought down by Jibrīl, upon him be peace, and I swear by these things that your companion is not mad," meaning by it the Prophet ﷺ, because they said: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِي نُـزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الذِّكْرُ إنَّكَ لَمَجْنُونٌ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 6], so He said: ﴿ن والقَلَمِ وما يَسْطُرُونَ﴾ [al-Qalam: 1] ﴿ما أنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾ [al-Qalam: 2], and He said in this place: ﴿وَما صاحِبُكم بِمَجْنُونٍ﴾.
﴿وَلَقَدْ رَآهُ بِالأُفُقِ المُبِينِ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 23]: we have explained that in Sūrat al-Najm.

zajjaj:24-24.t: ﴿وَما هو عَلى الغَيْبِ بِضَنِينٍ﴾ — it is also read «بِظَنِينٍ». Whoever read «بِظَنِينٍ», its meaning is: he is not suspect regarding the unseen; he is trustworthy in what he conveyed from Allah, Majestic and Mighty. One says «ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا» in the sense of «اِتَّهَمْتُ زَيْدًا» ("I suspected Zayd"). Whoever read ﴿بِضَنِينٍ﴾, its meaning is: "he is not niggardly regarding the unseen", that is: he ﷺ conveys from Allah and teaches the Book of Allah.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿فَأيْنَ تَذْهَبُونَ﴾: its meaning is: "So what road will you take that is clearer than this way which I have made clear to you?!"

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿لِمَن شاءَ مِنكم أنْ يَسْتَقِيمَ﴾, that is: uprightness is clear to you, so whoever wishes takes the road of truth and moderation, which is faith in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger. Then He informed them that the will regarding granting success (tawfīq) belongs to Him, and that they are not able to do that except by the will of Allah and His granting of success, saying: ﴿وَما تَشاءُونَ إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ رَبُّ العالَمِينَ﴾ [al-Takwīr: 29]. A further proof of that is: ﴿وَما تَوْفِيقِي إلا بِاللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ﴾ [Hūd: 88]. This is a notification that man does no good except by Allah's granting of success, and no evil except by Allah's forsaking him, because good and evil are by His decree and His measuring: He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills, as He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿اللَّهُ يَجْتَبِي إلَيْهِ مَن يَشاءُ ويَهْدِي إلَيْهِ مَن يُنِيبُ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 13].
